rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders 2:2 as “that Book,” free of doubt and the very guidance for the God-conscious.
rows.anchor: İşte o kitap, bunda şüphe yok, ʿayn-ı hidâyet, korunacaklar için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufans count some opening letters as verses, making al-Baqara’s ALM its disputed first verse; Basrans count none of these initials as verses.
rows.anchor: Bu ta‘dâd Kûfiyyûn rivayetidir. Basriyyûn yirmi dokuz sûrede bulunan işbu mukatta‘âttan hiçbirini bir âyet olarak saymamışlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse enumeration is transmitted rather than analogical, so disagreement over counting the initials resembles differences in Qur’anic readings.
rows.anchor: Âyet meselesi kıyâsî değil tevkīfî bir ilim olduğundan bu ihtilâf vücûh-i kırâat gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although written as one word, ALM is recited as three words, the meaningful names of the simple letters they denote.
rows.anchor: “Elif Lâm Mîm” diye üç kelime olarak okunuyor. Bu üç kelime mânalı birer isimdirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alphabetic letters are fundamentally individual sounds; their written shapes are signs representing those sounds.
rows.anchor: Her isim, başındaki ilk sesin veya nakşın adı, her nakış da bizzat o seslerin bir nevi resmidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic has twenty-eight original letters grounded in definite points of articulation, each with a name and a simple written form.
rows.anchor: muhakkaka müstenid aslî olarak yirmi sekiz harf ve bunların yirmi sekiz de ismi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds an implicit letter, lâm alif, usually called alif while the other is hamza; it is a lengthening letter with three forms, yielding twenty-nine actual and thirty-one counted letter names.
rows.anchor: buna da “lâm elif” denilir. Ve ‘ale’l-ekser “elif” ismi buna verildiğinden diğerine “hemze” denilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Letters in isolation are named and written as the alphabet, while combined forms use abjad; ALM is written like abjad but read alphabetically, combining both qualities as a fuller title for the letters.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki الم ebced gibi yazıldığı hâlde elifba gibi okunur. Demek ki ikisinin de haysiyetini câmi‘olarak hurûf-i hecânın daha mükemmel bir unvanı gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its meaning is clear when heard as letter names, but its writing resembles an opaque, obscure abjad word.
rows.anchor: Okunuşuna nazaran mânası sarihtir. Fakat yazılışına nazaran ebced gibi mühmel ve mübhem bir kelime görünür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If read as written in abjad fashion, possible forms such as alamma, alam, or ilamma could make a meaningful word; this makes a direct meaning harder to identify.
rows.anchor: Gerçi yazılış elifba gibi okunmayıp ebced gibi okunsa idi اَلَمَّ,اَلَمْ, اِلَمَّ ilh… vücûh-i muhtemelesiyle mânalı bir kelime teşkil edecekti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction of these two qualities suggests that the initials bear both an outward and an inward meaning.
rows.anchor: Bu iki haysiyetin böyle ictimâ‘ından yek nazarda anlaşılır ki burada biri zâhir, biri bâtın iki mâna melhuzdur.

rows.speaker: bir kısmı
rows.claim: Exegetes divide over whether the intended meaning of the disjointed initials can be known; some hold that it cannot.
rows.anchor: bir kısmı da olamayacağına kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: ma‘lûmiyet veya imkân-ı ma‘lûmiyete zâhib olanlar
rows.claim: The first knowability camp takes the names as meaningful and their enumeration as a reminder of the alphabet and abjad, drawing attention to language as the material of the Book and announcing a challenge to Qur’anic inimitability.
rows.anchor: Ma‘lûmiyet veya imkân-ı ma‘lûmiyete zâhib olanlar başlıca iki zümre teşkil ediyorlar: 1. Bu isimlerin mânaları mâlumdur.

rows.speaker: ekser-i ulemâ
rows.claim: Most scholars in the knowability camp also prefer that the three letters together are a name for this sura or the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: Ve bu zümredeki ekser-i ulemâ, bu üç harfin mecmû‘u bu sûreye veya Kur’ân’a

rows.speaker: ikinci zümre
rows.claim: The second camp seeks the intended meaning in the letters’ referents, their combination, or their written form rather than in the three spoken names, allowing a symbolic meaning.
rows.anchor: Ma‘nâ-yı murâdın kelimât-ı selâsede değil müsemmeyâtında, yani

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an example of abbreviation, an unnamed poet has a speaker abbreviate وَقَفْتُ to the letter qāf in the line about telling a woman to stop.
rows.anchor: şâirin قُلْتُ لَهَا قِفِي فَقَالَتْ قَاف mısrâında olduğu gibi وَقَفْتُ kelimesinden kāf harfiyle iktifâ etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another abbreviation example is writing an initial alif in place of the name Ahmad.
rows.anchor: kitabette misâli de meselâ “Ahmed” yerinde bir ا (elif) yazılması bu kabîldendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Letters may hint at names through their initial, final, or middle positions; he notes that الر, حم, ن can be combined into the divine name al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: الر,حم,ن cem edildiği zaman اَلرَّحْمنُ isminin hâsıl olduğu görülüyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further symbolic approach reads the initials through the numerical calculation and cipher method of abjad.
rows.anchor: İkincisi ebcedin hesap tarîki ve şifre usulüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the possible approaches must be considered together, but their meanings then remain ambiguous and the intended meaning cannot be fixed.
rows.anchor: Bunda ise me‘ânî müteşabih olur. Ta‘yîn-i murâda imkân bulunamaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ALM suggests a “known-unknown” whose meaning reaches divine realities and names, ending in “God knows best”; it teaches that human knowledge begins before an origin whose essence cannot be grasped.
rows.anchor: الم sanki el-ma‘lûmü’l-mechûl terkîbi gibi bir mâna ifade eder. Ve bu mâna hakikat ve esmâ-i ilâhiyeye kadar gider.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı refuses to discard any interpretive perspective on rational or transmitted grounds, since the initials’ recitation and overall pattern strongly support the first approach.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-hakīka hem dirâyeten ve hem rivayeten bu nokta-i nazarların hiçbirini feda etmeye imkân yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initials occur in twenty-nine suras, matching the twenty-nine alphabet letters; fourteen names, half of the twenty-eight, were selected to represent the letters’ attribute classes and original pronunciation and tajwid.
rows.anchor: Elifba gibi okunan mukatta‘ât-ı süver, evvelâ elifba harflerinin yirmi dokuz sayısına müsâvi olarak yirmi dokuz sûrede mevcuddur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourteen selected names form half the alphabet and cover halves or important members of its different categories, thereby representing the full set in its original pronunciation and tajwid; al-Qadi’s tafsir also states these patterns, whose details Elmalılı omits.
rows.anchor: yirmi sekiz ismin tam nısfı bulunan on dört harf ismi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distribution of the initials across suras reflects Arabic morphology and syntax: word classes, one-to-five-letter patterns, unaugmented and augmented forms, the seven-letter ceiling, and root versus attached forms of quadriliteral and quinqueliteral words.
rows.anchor: Kelimenin aksâm-ı selâsesi, birliden beşliye kadar kelimâtın ebniye-i asliyesi, mücerred ve mezîd taksîmâtı, mezîd binâsının yedi harfi tecavüz edemeyeceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı argues that it is implausible for an unlettered prophet to present such precise linguistic insights before these sciences formed, especially when the initials later guided the establishment of linguistic rules; this supports Qur’anic inimitability.
rows.anchor: bir nebiyy-i ümmî teblîğiyle dekāik-i ilmiyeye ait ibraz edilen ve bilâhare kavâ‘id-i lisâniyenin vaz‘-ı esâsında büyük bir rehber olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high significance cannot be restricted to outward indications, since doing so conflicts with the evidence and neglects many aspects; the intended meaning combines outward and inward, alphabetic and abjad perspectives.
rows.anchor: vücûh-ı delâletten birçoğunu ihmal eylemek demektir. Binâen‘aleyh asıl ma‘nâ-yı murâd zâhir ve bâtın, elifba ve ebced nokta-i nazarlarının cem‘indedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initials’ benefit is to move the reader from verbal signs through rational, natural, and intuitive meanings toward the first source and hidden reality, then to acknowledge human incapacity and await divine guidance; this is the limitless trial of the firmly grounded.
rows.anchor: işte müteşabihât denilen mukatta‘ât-ı süverin fâide-i hitâbı “ibtilâ-i râsihîn” denilen bu nâmütenâhî mânada müncelîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human reality is perception and communication: perception occurs through meanings, communication through words, and words through sounds, which together are the pillars of language.
rows.anchor: İdrak bizzat me‘ânî ile, teblîğ-i idrâk da kelimât ile, kelimât ise asvât ile cereyan eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing is “the language of language,” and language and writing are the foundation of human intellectual and practical progress.
rows.anchor: Kitabet ise lisânü’l-lisân demektir. Ve bu sebeple lisan ve kitabet beşeriyette terakkiyât-ı ilmiye ve ameliyenin mebnâ-yı aslîsidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A language is more advanced when its alphabet is fixed and orderly, pronunciation precise, morphology and syntax robust, meanings broad and deep, and spelling stable.
rows.anchor: elifba harfleri denilen asvât-ı müfrede ve basîta bütün lisanların maddesi, bunların eşkâl-i hattıyeleri de kitabetin üssü’l-esâsıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an, revealed from its beginning with a call to reading and writing, awakens consciousness through al-Fatiha and then begins with the alphabet, the material of language.
rows.anchor: ta bidayetinde kıraat ve kitabete terğīb emriyle nâzil olmaya başlayan Kur’ân-ı azîmü’ş-şân’ın Fâtiha ile şuurları uyandırdıktan sonra madde-i lisân olan hurûf-i hecâdan başlaması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı reads ALM’s written form as proclaiming true divine unity against the Christian Trinity while showing the derivative duality of God and world, or spirit and body.
rows.anchor: hakīkīden ve vâhid-i i‘tibârî olan ikiyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also says the initials allude to the supreme name of the deity whom Jewish tradition treats as one whose name is not spoken.
rows.anchor: Yahudiliğin “ismi söylenmez” diye tanıdığı Ma‘bûd-ı ekberin ism-i a‘zamına da telmih etmiş olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters lead from the back of the throat to the lips through three articulation points that encompass the letters’ full articulation.
rows.anchor: aksâ-yı sîneden dudağın ucuna kadar bütün hurûfun mehâric-i külliyesine muntabık üç mahreçten tertîb-i mahsus ile çıkarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the opening letters also point to the Stoic philosophers’ “alphabet proof” for the existence of God.
rows.anchor: “elifba delîli” tâbir edilen isbât-ı ilâh delîline de işaret etmiş bulunması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book guides human thought from sounds to words, meanings, things, the mystery of creation, the first principle of existence, and divine knowledge, thus guiding humanity from beginning to end.
rows.anchor: akıl ve fikr-i beşeri sırr-ı lisân içinde asvâttan kelimâta, kelimâttan me‘ânîye, me‘ânîden eşyâya, eşyâdan sırr-ı tekvîne

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He exhorts the thinker to pronounce ALM with attention to articulation and to listen inwardly to the sounds emerging from the self, weighing and recognizing oneself through them.
rows.anchor: Ey mütefekkir! الم remzine bak ve mehâric-i hurûfa riayet ederek “elif lâm mîm” diye oku, okurken kendini bir tart;

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simple, individually meaningless sounds yield countless meanings in words, discourse, and books expressing the cosmos; contemplating this sequence reveals creative power and the mystery of existence.
rows.anchor: hiçbir mânası olmayan bu münferid ve basit seslerden, lâ-yuhsâ mânayı hâmil olan kelimelerin ve bu kelimelerden kelâmların ve bu kelâmlardan kâinatı ifade eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every meaning, blessing, advance, perfection, and hope depends on a properly ordered social system.
rows.anchor: âlemde her mâna, her feyz, her terakki, her kemâl, her ümit bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îye, hem de vaz‘-ı lâyıkıyla bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îye medyundur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When simple material components are put in their proper order, they produce chemistry, wisdom, structures, and life, forming the visible cosmos.
rows.anchor: mevâdd-ı basîta eczâ-i münferidesi lâyık oldukları bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îyi buldukları zaman onlardan kimyâlar, hikmetler, heyetler, hayatlar fışkırarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, properly ordered human individuals form societies, nations, and states that travel and conquer, spread truth and justice, and attain happiness.
rows.anchor: insan ferdleri de yerli yerinde mükemmel bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘îye mazhar oldukları zaman da onlardan dünyaları teshir eden hey’et-i ictimâ‘iyeler, milletler, devletler meydana gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order that gives simple letters countless meanings is a key to creation; existence from nonexistence, meaning from the meaningless, and distinct parts forming a whole prove an eternal, encompassing power of divine unity, leaving no basis for doubt.
rows.anchor: böyle ma‘dûmun mevcud, mânasızın mânalı olabilmesi, ayrı ve müteferrik şeylerin birleşip bir kül teşkil edebilmeleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He urges the reader to seek a firm, upright social order from the generous source and submit inwardly and outwardly to it to find guidance and happiness.
rows.anchor: o menba‘-ı cûddan kendin için de metîn ve müstakīm bir nizâm-ı ictimâ‘î aramalısın, bâtın ve zâhirinle ona ‘arz-ı teslîmiyet etmelisin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should not try to encompass God’s essence, knowledge, or power; at that limit one must confess incapacity and ignorance, recite ALM and “God knows best,” and seek refuge in humble supplication.
rows.anchor: Fakat sakın O’nun hakikatine ereceğim, O’nu ve O’nun ilm u kudretini ihâta edeceğim diye uğraşma. O noktaya geldiğin zaman acz u cehlini itiraf et.
